2026-11-16.summary: Whiplashed all morning. Bought in multiple times on wrong entries and added without confirmation. Limits felt slow — price ran past the order, so I chased. Stops too tight for the chop. Lost $166, way past my threshold. Felt like I was carrying too much money and I went past my 8-trade sweet spot.
2026-11-16.right: Spotted the problems myself the same day and wrote rules for them. Last put (P662) held 38 min for +$64.
2026-11-16.fix: Mondays = paper. 8 trades max then close Webull. Stops $0.15–0.20. Only enter with the 20-min candle, max 2 entries per candle. Limit at ask + $0.02–0.03, skip if it ran $0.10 past.

2026-11-17.summary: Woke up late and was right place, right time. Stayed at 1 contract on purpose after yesterday. Caught the big put move I knew was coming, then sat through the chop and kept the bulk of it. Could have made more with 2 or by holding, but I'm in account-recovery mode. $1,800 in the account stressed me out — going to hold it around $1,250 and withdraw weekly.
2026-11-17.right: P651 held 11 min for +$206 — the move I planned for. Size stayed at 1. Finished green +$172.
2026-11-17.fix: 11 trades (cap is 8). 4 losers in a row 8:03–8:21 and kept going. Flipped puts↔calls within a minute at 8:21.

2026-11-18.summary: Struggled. No direction — price kept getting bought up, just a slow grind down, and calls got eaten up quickly. Gave back a big chunk of my first trade and didn't respect my rules. Still ended green, but non-direction days like this kill me every time.
2026-11-18.right: Read the open: P649 6:34 +$87 and the add at 6:35 +$53 — up +$114 by 6:47. Stops stayed small (median ~$0.15). Finished green.
2026-11-18.fix: Peaked +$114 at 6:47 and gave back $68 — the $45 giveback rule would have ended the day around +$70. 17 trades (cap 8): 12 more after the high, mostly calls↔puts every few minutes in chop. On a no-direction day, once you hit +$60 and the candles alternate colors, close Webull.

2026-11-19.summary: Absolute chaos. Went in like Bambi with heavy size (2 contracts), ran out of cash and had to use unsettled funds (good-faith violation risk on Webull). When it was time to add size I didn't, then got scared holding — the put went to about $6.00 and I left with about half of it.
2026-11-19.right: The 7:10 P659 caught the real move: 0.75 -> 3.73, +$298, held 22 minutes. Opening call at 6:30 +$33. Ended green +$161.
2026-11-19.fix: Down -$137 by 7:10 after 10 trades in 40 minutes, mostly 2 contracts, flipping 682 calls / 660 puts and two far-OTM 687 calls (-$53). That broke the -$75 stop — the day was saved by the trade that broke it, which is luck, not a plan. Size only after a green trade, never on the first ones. Keep cash settled so you never need unsettled funds.

2026-11-20.summary: Practice day — testing the range levels on purpose. Yes, too many trades, but I was testing levels. Took a call that won, then jumped in at the right level for the put dump, but didn't realise how much cash I'd used, so I had to buy a really far out-of-the-money put. It still paid. I was okay with how it went — still practicing.
2026-11-20.right: Two real reads made +$330: the 6:51 C650 caught the 636 → 643 pop (+$88, added into a winner), and the 7:07 P621 ×2 at 0.37 caught the dump after the failed push at 643 — held 19 min with a raised stop, sold 1.58 (+$242). Every stop $0.15 or tighter, no chasing. Ended +$199.
2026-11-20.fix: Testing the $634–638 chop cost −$128 over 12 tries and broke the −$75 stop by 6:49 (−$85); 7 entries in each of the first two 20-min candles. Practice rule: 1 contract, 2 tries, then wait — the tests cost ~$30 and the cash is still there for the real setup.

2026-11-23.summary: THE $500 DAY. I told myself not to trade today. QQQ moved about $40 in pre-market, I got pulled in anyway, and it turned into a slow-grind range day: the slowest grind to the top and the weakest pull back down. I kept thinking we were going to break out. I knew I was being tricked and kept trading because I couldn't admit the market was weak today. Moved my stop to 0.30, went to 3 contracts to win it back, kept going with $1 wicks and IV around 60%. Broke my good-faith limit and used all my cash. Gave back all of last week (+$414) and more. Remember how this felt. NOTE TO FUTURE ME: Because of ego and refusing to admit I was wrong, I put my future, my hard work and my mental health at risk — and I'm the one who has to deal with it now. Get a grip. $500 for what? Don't ever risk that much again. Don't ever get tricked again. If you take a trade, it's because of auction mechanics — never because you're chasing a lotto.
2026-11-23.right: Every stop actually filled — the stops did their job; the damage was getting back in. I did stop eventually once I saw it was pure revenge on a dead range. And I'm writing it down so I never pay for this lesson twice.
2026-11-23.fix: 16 entries, 0 winners, −$505. The −$75 daily stop broke at 6:43 — 13 minutes in; everything after it cost −$405. 8 entries in the 6:30–6:50 candle, 6 in the next. Flipped call/put 2–13 seconds after a stop. Added to a losing C665 (0.55 → 0.58 → 0.70) and rode it to 0.27 (−$102). Market orders at the end out of anger (P638 ×3 −$120, C658 −$37). RULES FROM TODAY: (1) a no-trade day means Webull stays closed. (2) Big pre-market gap = no entries for the first 30 minutes — the move already happened. (3) Hit −$75 = close the app, no exceptions. (4) Never add to a loser. (5) Settled cash only — no more good-faith violations. (6) Only take a trade because of auction mechanics — never a lotto.

2026-11-24.summary: Day after the $500 day. I kept trying to win back my $500 loss and I wasn't trading correctly. I loaded $600 during the session just so I could keep trying. Ping-pong morning: a $6 box from 6:30 to 7:15, candles moving so slow that decay killed my options. I held the P625 puts for so long — I knew it was dead and I couldn't let it go. I felt mad and like a loser, like how I used to feel before I was profitable. Down −$318 before one trade (C640 ×4 at 9:06) brought it back to green.
2026-11-24.right: Every stop was clean at about −$0.15 and never moved. Probes were 1 contract. My reads were right: the 7:15–8:15 grind down (P625) and the 9:06 bounce off 633 (C640). I saw the reversal, punched it, and sold it at 2.13 — +$456. Finished green +$138.
2026-11-24.fix: Daily stop −$75 was hit at 6:41 (6th probe); I was −$318 before the last trade. 12 probes in 28 minutes, 9 in the first 20-min candle (max 2). The first 15 minutes went nowhere (−$0.20) = range-day warning. P625 ×3 each reached +$0.30 and peaked 1.31 at 7:49 (about +$219) — never sold, stopped at 0.35 for −$70. RULES: (1) let the $500 go — each day starts at zero, +$60 = done. (2) No deposits during market hours. (3) Flat first 15 minutes = range day, 2 probes max. (4) Up +$0.30 = the 3-min trail goes on, no exceptions. (5) Size up only after confirmation, never to win back a loss.

2026-11-25.summary: I was holding and I over-leveraged. I didn't cash out of a $140 trade and ended up −$160, then I took another trade, made my money back and then some, and then I gave back $100 because it was pinned at 610. I know I'm being stubborn because last week I didn't hold on those puts that went to $1,000 and that hurts. I'm very disappointed with my trading this week, and because of the $500 loss I'm not trading correctly. — The tape: QQQ gapped down $21 (638.10 → 617.10), flushed to 607.76 by 6:45, ripped to 619.38 at 7:00, dumped back to 610 by 7:27, then sat pinned 609–614. The 9th reversal morning in a row. Later: "The market is hard right now and I'm in negative drawdown, and it's hard to trade with a clear head. I was so good at taking profit with my levels, trail, +$30 — I had holes with overtrading — but for some reason I'm just trying to take moon shots in an environment where price is fighting to go back up, when we'll probably still be in this range for a couple of weeks."
2026-11-25.right: My reads were right twice. The C628 ×5 at 6:55–6:56 (0.56–0.64) caught the rip off the 607 low and I sold right at the 7:00 top: +$194. The P601 ×3 at 7:06–7:10 caught the dump: +$121. From −$155 at 6:54 I was +$145 by 7:22. Every exit was a stop order. After the pin I came back at 9:09–9:19 for 3 small calls (C625 ×2, C628): +$34. Finished +$89.
2026-11-25.fix: 1) P601 stacked to 5 contracts in 4 minutes (1.08 → 1.21 → 1.40 ×2) at the open and held through the flush low instead of taking the +$140 — all 4 stopped at 0.93 at 6:54 for −$137. On a reversal tape, +0.30 = the 3-min trail goes on. 2) After +$145 at 7:20 I gave back $90 in the 609–614 pin: 5 more entries, ending with P594 ×4 at market at 7:51 (0.33 → 0.15, −$72). Pinned = done for the day. 3) 16 entries, up to 5 contracts at once. Regret from last week's $1,000 puts is steering the holding — let the trail decide, not regret. 4) Let the $500 go: each day starts at zero. 5) The 9:09–9:19 trades were on unsettled cash (settled cash −$509 at 9:20) — good-faith violation risk. Settled cash only until it resets. 6) Back to what worked: levels + trail + take +$30. No moon shots in a reversal tape — past stretches like this took about 4 weeks (17–37 mornings) to return to normal.

2026-11-27.summary: Day after Thanksgiving (market closes 10:00 PT). Light was 🔥 CAREFUL (+19.9). QQQ gapped up $11.79 (633.93 → 645.72), sold off $9 to 636.72 by 7:05, chopped 637–642 until 7:30, then ripped to 646.61 by 7:47. In my words: "I definitely got caught in chop. I noticed that sizing up with a market order gets me in during the rip — but I also noticed it buying really late sometimes. I was calm after the drawdown, which made me happy, because I was able to focus on price instead of picking a winner. I noticed the box, but the chop was horrendous."
2026-11-27.right: Opened with the gap-fade: P634 ×3 at 6:32–6:34, sold into the flush for +$65. Then the trade of the day: C645 ×4 at 1.17 at 7:35 on the rip, sold at 2.02 at 7:38 for +$340 — sized up only once the move was proving itself. Every loser after 6:44 was a clean $0.13–0.16 stop. Finished +$127 (+$124.51 after fees).
2026-11-27.fix: 1) 6:37–7:27: 16 entries in the 637–642 chop, flipping calls and puts every few minutes (C645 ×6, P632 ×4, P629 ×3): −$278. Chop after the first move = sit until it breaks. 2) P632 ×2 at 1.43 at 6:39 added above the first P632 at 1.02 and stopped at 1.01: −$84, the day's biggest loss. 3) The C645 ×4 was sold at +0.85 — the ladder would have held it into 646.61. 4) 18 entries; the plan is 8. 5) Market orders: great for getting in on a confirmed rip, but they can fill late — use them only after the break is proven, never inside the box.
